floor_history.headline: Object-model fix (D_800A9CF8 header struct, base+offset evidence) drops honest floor 40 -> 13; loop body byte-exact; residual is pre-loop sched1/local-alloc coupling fully attributed (birthing-leaf re
Residual fully localised to ONE sched1 birthing_insn_p boost; form A3 measures the allocation half at 13 with the target's 49-instruction count and the target's register seats.

frontier.hypothesis: Form C needs ONLY reg_n_sets[src] >= 2 at flow time (or src not live at block-0 exit); every other byte it produces is already the target's, so this is the cheapest close.
frontier.mechanism: Without the birthing boost the store wins T-2 by potential_hazard, the src copy then beats the address insn at T-3 on LUID, the address insn takes T-4 and the count load T-5, giving forward order count/addr/copy/store with the copy a deleted $v0<-$v0 no-op.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver on block 0 of the s1 dumpsC pre-sched chain and have it enumerate the minimal insn-attribute change that flips T-2 to the store, then run tools/ra_solver inverse_compose.py classify on the resulting seat assignment. Do this BEFORE spelling more C - twenty spellings across two sessions have now landed on 13.

frontier.hypothesis: Form A closes if the pre-check count pseudo is NOT remapped by duplicate_loop_exit_test, because the copied load would then set the same pseudo as the in-loop load and reg_n_sets would be 2, removing its boost at T-4.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c:2163 remaps only when regno_first_uid[reg] is the exit-test insn AND regno_last_uid[reg] is inside the exit code; a loop shape in which the bound temp is referenced outside the exit code skips the remap.
frontier.next_probe: Re-read duplicate_loop_exit_test with the loop body in hand, construct one or two ordinary loop shapes whose bound temp escapes the exit code, and CHECK reg_n_sets in the .flow dump before spending a sandbox run.

frontier.hypothesis: A3 already has the target's schedule, seats and instruction count (49); only the hoisted anchor is wrong. Any ordinary-C form that keeps A3's schedule while materialising &D_800A9CF8+0x10 before the dst load closes the function.
frontier.mechanism: cse/loop relate the LICM-hoisted &D_800A9CF8 to the first register-form address of the object in the function; with the dst load first that is &D+0xC, so the store falls back to a symbol-direct sw through $at.
frontier.next_probe: Diff A3's .cse2/.loop dumps against A0's to see exactly which insn establishes the anchor, then look for a statement shape that needs the +0x10 address first without reintroducing the address insn that beat the copy at T-3 in A0.
